description: A family olive and herb farm. Visitors walk the groves, see the stone olive press, pick za'atar and sage, and finish with a home-cooked lunch in the courtyard.

stops.name: Welcome & tea
facts: The farm has been in my family for four generations.
Tea is sage tea from herbs grown on the farm.

stops.name: Olive grove
facts: There are about 600 olive trees; the oldest are estimated to be over 300 years old.
Harvest runs from mid-October to December, and visitors can join the harvest on Saturday tours.
The trees are rain-fed with no irrigation.

stops.name: Stone olive press
facts: The press is a traditional stone mill, still used for small batches.
About 5 kg of olives make 1 litre of oil.
Oil is cold-pressed and bottled the same week.

stops.name: Herb garden
facts: Za'atar, sage, mint and chamomile grow here.
Za'atar is dried in the shade for about ten days and mixed with sesame and sumac.

stops.name: Courtyard lunch
facts: Lunch is maqluba or musakhan depending on the day, cooked by my mother.
Vegetarian and gluten-free plates are available with one day's notice.

offers: Guests can join the olive harvest on Saturday tours from mid-October to December.
A 90-minute za'atar-making workshop can be added for 10 JOD per person.
The tour costs 25 JOD per adult including lunch; children under 12 are 12 JOD.
booking: Book by WhatsApp on the number on the farm card, at least one day ahead. Cash and CliQ payments are accepted.
